M_100_FR: Nearly all top performers breathe every stroke for most of the race.
One world-record swim skipped breathing the first 25m (12 strokes); another skipped breathing the last 15m.
M_200_FR: All of the men breathe every 2 strokes for the entire race.
M_100_FL: More men than ever are now using a breath-holding pattern in the 100 fly rather than breathing every stroke.
Only a small minority breathe every stroke through both 50s.
M_200_FL: About half hold a breathing pattern the entire race; the rest breathe every stroke throughout, or hold a pattern only for the first 50-100.
F_100_FR: Most have a breathing pattern, commonly breathing every 4 strokes for a significant part of the race.
A couple of top performers breathe every stroke but skip the final ~15-16m before the wall.
F_200_FR: Roughly a quarter hold a pattern the whole race, a quarter hold one just for the final 50, and about half breathe every stroke throughout.
F_100_FL: Most breathe 1-up-1-down on the first 50, then about half shift to 2-up-1-down on the second 50.
A rare few breathe every stroke, even into the final stroke.
F_200_FL: All hold a breathing pattern the entire race — most commonly 1-up-1-down, with some using 2-up-1-down or 3-up-1-down.
